The gap is caused by trimesh's face_adjacency requiring an edge to be used by exactly 2 faces, so it refuses to traverse link5's 139 four-face non-manifold edges at z = 80.551819. My label-by-label test proves the any-shared-edge partition and the shared-vertex partition are the SAME partition, so vertex-connectivity contributes nothing beyond edge-connectivity. This matters because the wrong mechanism licenses treating the 114 fragments as a benign definitional artefact, when they in fact mark a real un-booleaned CAD seam.

THE REVERIFY PHASE'S OWN REPAIR OF G0b ('window COUNT discriminates: moving = 1, fixed = 2'). Worse, the moving jaw's LARGEST cut-out is the slot at 168.7152 mm^2, and the fixed blade's window A at 277.8090 mm^2 is 1.6466x larger than even that - so 'which one has the bigger window' answers 'fixed' under every reading.

G0a AS A PHYSICAL HAND TEST. D2.2000 is exactly the ISO 273 close-fit clearance hole for M2, in a 1.5000 mm plate, on what the URDF proves are the GRIPPING faces (joint5 axis z in the child frame => tip velocity proportional to (5.2334, 67.0826, 0), so the jaw closes along +/-y and the y-normal web faces these bores pierce are the contact faces). These are through-bolt holes DESIGNED to carry hardware, and hypothesis C is precisely the case where the hardware is still fitted. Every standard M2 part hides the hole and presents a larger disc: ISO 4762 cap head D3.8000 (0.8000 mm radial overhang), ISO 4032 nut across corners D4.3800, ISO 7089 washer OD D5.0000. Occupy both bores - 2 of 2 = 100% of the positive evidence - and the moving jaw's visible bore set collapses to {3.2 x3}, which is exactly the fixed blade's signature. A negative test whose failure mode IS the hypothesis under test cannot arbitrate that hypothesis.

THE REVERIFY PHASE'S OWN REPAIR OF G0a ('measure the 21.00 mm PITCH rather than the diameter'). link5 carries a D2.0000 bore pair at EXACTLY 20.5000 mm centre pitch - I reproduced 20.5000000000 independently, three such pairs. Caliper margin is 0.7000 mm outside-to-outside (23.2000 vs 22.5000) and only 0.3000 mm inside-to-inside (18.8000 vs 18.5000). Asking a human to resolve 0.3000 mm across two burred hole edges is not a categorical test. Honest scope note: all eight D2.0 bores are proximal (nearest at z = 43.7356, 8.2994 mm below the joint plane), so this confounder bites only if the detached part carried wrist-yoke material - which, per the next item, is undetermined.

'D2.2 vs D3.2 IS RESOLVABLE BY EYE OR BY A DRILL SHANK'. The bore is only 1.5000 mm deep, so its mouth chamfer dominates what an eye or a caliper's inside knife-edges contacts. Apparent mouth diameter = 2.2000 + 2c: a 0.2500 mm break-edge (a routine deburr call-out) makes it read 2.7000, the exact midpoint between the two families; 0.3000 mm makes it read 2.8000, already closer to 3.2000 than to its own nominal; 0.5000 mm makes it read exactly 3.2000. A pin/shank gauge is immune to chamfer but has an inverted failure: the entire margin to link5's D2.0000 family is 0.2000 mm on diameter = 0.1000 mm of radius, inside a single coating layer. Chamfer defeats the visual branch, coating defeats the gauge branch.

'G0a AND G0b ARE TWO INDEPENDENT CHECKS'. They are collocated on ONE surface: both D2.2 bores (x = 38.3042) and the entire window (x in [45.2042, 60.3907]) pierce the same y-normal web faces, which are the gripping faces. A single 23.1865 x 28.2949 mm pad covering all three features hides 100% of BOTH discriminators - 62.17% of the 1055.3261 mm^2 web silhouette. The geometry even supplies a ready-made pad pocket: the -y web face is recessed 4.0162 mm below the fork-plate edges across a 36.3676 mm channel. And a pad is not speculative - the two M2 holes at 21.0000 pitch IN THE GRIPPING FACE are what a pad is mounted with, so the very feature G0a keys on is evidence that a pad belongs there. Any two-screw pad respecting a conventional 1.5xD edge margin is at least 27.6000 mm long = 97.54% of the window's z-extent.

korean_briefing: ■ 이번에 무엇을 왜 했는가 — 지난 세션에 13개 에이전트로 이루어진 '적대 패널'(서로 반박하도록 설계한 검증 팀)을 띄웠는데, 5개 중 4개가 네트워크 오류(ENOTIMP)로 도중에 죽었습니다. 살아남은 1개(synthesizer, 종합자)는 자기 입으로 '나는 렌즈 보고서를 하나도 못 받았다'고 적었습니다. 그런데 그 1인이 쓴 숫자가 지금 START_HERE.md와 37차 세션 문서에 '사실'로 들어가 있습니다. 이번 작업은 그 숫자들을 (1) 죽은 에이전트들의 기록에서 건져내고, (2) 제가 직접 처음부터 다시 계산하고, (3) 일부러 깨뜨리려 드는 반박자 3명을 붙여서 검증한 것입니다.

■ 가장 먼저, 흔들리지 않는 것 하나 — 움직이는 조(gripper_link.stl) 부품의 '볼록껍질 지름'은 **81.4065mm**입니다. 볼록껍질(convex hull)이란 부품 전체를 고무줄로 감쌌을 때 생기는 가장 바깥 껍데기를 말하고, 그 지름은 **그 부품에서 두 점을 아무리 멀리 잡아도 나올 수 없는 절대 최대 길이**입니다. 이 숫자는 이제 서로 완전히 다른 5개의 계산 경로(죽은 렌즈의 손으로 짠 바이트 파서, 재도출 2명, 반박자 1명, 그리고 저)에서 소수점 끝자리까지 똑같이 나왔고, 반박자가 일부러 깨려고 공격했는데도 살아남았습니다. 86.4는 이 값을 4.9935mm, 즉 6.1340% 초과합니다. **단, 이건 '부품에 대한 사실'이지 '86.4에 대한 사실'이 아닙니다** — 아래 마지막 항목을 꼭 보십시오.

■ 가장 큰 수정 1 — 가설 D를 죽였다던 숫자가 틀렸고, 방향까지 반대였습니다. 문서에는 '관절축 평면(z=52.035)에서 고정측 조를 재면 67.2433mm밖에 안 되니 86.4에 19.1567mm 모자라서 D는 사망'이라고 적혀 있습니다. 두 가지 결함이 겹쳐 있었습니다. 첫째, '정점 필터'(vertex filter, 평면 위쪽에 있는 꼭짓점만 골라 쓰는 방식)를 썼는데 이러면 평면을 걸치고 있는 삼각형이 통째로 버려집니다. 이 부품의 거친 판에서는 그 사각지대가 3.9721mm나 됩니다. 둘째, 부피의 74%를 차지하는 덩어리 하나를 **아무 설명 없이 빼고** 계산했습니다. 제가 '면 클리핑'(face clipping, 삼각형을 평면에서 정확히 잘라 절단면 교점까지 넣는 정공법)으로 다시 재니 **74.3076mm**(모자란 양 12.0924mm)였습니다. 같은 문서 117번째 줄에는 같은 평면에 대해 69.7673이라고 적혀 있어서, 문서가 자기 자신과 이미 모순되고 있었습니다.

■ 가장 큰 수정 2 (이번 작업에서 제일 중요합니다) — **가설 D를 배제한 논리 자체가 방향이 거꾸로였습니다.** 원래 논리는 '고정측 조가 86.4를 만들기엔 너무 짧다'였습니다. 짧으면 어떻게 잡아도 86.4가 안 나오니까 이게 맞다면 정말 치명적입니다. 그런데 그 '짧음'은 z=52.035에서 자른다는 **가정** 위에서만 나옵니다. 실제로 파일을 열어보면 그 자리에는 부품 경계가 **아예 없습니다**. 자산이 정의하는 유일한 경계는 삼각형 7250개로 된 '닫힌 껍데기'(열린 모서리 0개 — 제가 직접 세었습니다)이고, 그 길이는 **103.8000mm**, 볼록껍질 지름은 **105.6842mm**입니다. 86.4는 그 안쪽으로 각각 17.4000mm, 19.2842mm 들어와 있습니다. 즉 **너무 짧은 게 아니라 너무 깁니다.** 긴 부품에서 86.4가 나오는 건 재는 지점만 달리 잡아도 쉽게 설명됩니다. 결론: **가설 D는 지금 가진 자산으로는 배제되지 않습니다.** 문서에 적힌 '사망' 판정을 뒤집어야 합니다.

■ 가장 큰 수정 3 — 사용자에게 드리려던 두 가지 손 검사(G0a, G0b)가 **둘 다 반증되었고, 더 나쁜 건 둘 다 같은 방향으로 틀린다는 점**입니다. G0a는 '부품에 지름 2.2mm 구멍이 있으면 움직이는 조'라는 검사입니다. 그런데 그 2.2mm는 M2 나사가 헐겁게 지나가라고 뚫은 **표준 나사 통과 구멍**이고, 그것도 하필 **물건을 집는 면**에 뚫려 있습니다(URDF의 관절 정의에서 조가 닫히는 방향을 계산해 확인했습니다). 즉 나사나 패드가 끼워져 있는 게 오히려 정상 상태이고, 그게 바로 가설 C가 말하는 상황입니다. honest_limits: THE FRAMING WAS NOT FIXED, ONLY FLAGGED. Every millimetre inference in this report - the protrusion family (5.2218 / 5.3459 / 8.5500 / 9.7177), the transcription rival, the cut-plane series, the C-prime thickness cap - presupposes 86.4 is a length. The no-caliper photo finding removes the warrant for that presupposition and I did not repair it; I only re-scoped the work to claims that hold either way. I did not look at the photos myself. The instrument's identity is a question only the user can answer, and it sits upstream of roughly half this document.

MY SCOPE WAS DELIBERATELY NARROW AND THAT LEAVES REAL GAPS. I re-derived asset geometry. I did not test anything physical, did not re-audit the s = 0.985 +/- 0.012 scale posterior (taken as given from the 35th session; deriving s from bores or plate thickness is a banned method), did not re-derive the 36th session's caliper protocol P0-P10, and did not re-examine the ten photographs. Claims resting on those - notably anything quoted in sigma against s - inherit whatever their original provenance was worth.

THE FORBIDDEN ASSET IS THE CHEAPEST WAY TO OVERTURN MY STRONGEST SURVIVING CLAIM. gripper_left_link.stl is referenced zero times in roarm_m3.urdf yet sits in the same mesh directory. If the user's part corresponds to it, then 'link5 has no D2.2 bore' - the one asset-level discriminator that survived every attack - was never tested against the relevant geometry. I did not open, load, hash, stat, list or size-infer it, and I stop at UNVERIFIABLE rather than reason around it.

'CONFIRMED' MEANS DIFFERENT THINGS FOR DIFFERENT ITEMS AND I HAVE TRIED TO SAY WHICH. Only a few claims were both independently re-derived AND explicitly targeted by a refuter who then failed: the 81.4065 ceiling (attacked by refuter-2, survived), the D2.2 asset facts (attacked by refuter-1, survived as asset geometry while failing as a hand test), and the four tip equalities (attacked by refuter-2, who conceded plainly). The rest were re-derived by two or more independent paths but never adversarially targeted. Multiple agreeing re-derivations are weaker evidence than a survived attack, because agents that share a method share its blind spots - the five agreeing computations of 9.0616 are the cautionary example: all arithmetically right, all measuring something the label did not describe.

I FOUND AND FIXED ONE ERROR OF MY OWN, AND THERE MAY BE OTHERS. My D2.0000 bore scan recovered 14 of the 16 expected rim loops - two loops were dropped by my chaining routine - so my raw output implied 7 bores where the correct count is 8 (4 + 2 + 2). I caught this only by cross-checking against refuter-1's plate-by-plate breakdown, and I report it rather than quietly publishing 7. My window waist sweep also produced a spurious zero-width reading at exactly z = -18.9336 where the scan line grazes a horizontal edge; the five-bead reading with four waists is correct and that artefact is mine.

TWO NUMBERS IN THIS REPORT REMAIN CONVENTION-DEPENDENT RATHER THAN SETTLED, AND I HAVE NOT PICKED A WINNER. (a) The fastener-free band around z = 52.035 is 39.9900 mm if you count only small fasteners (D <= 5) or 32.0162 mm if you count the D10/D13.566 counterbore stack at z = 75.7518 as the upper bound. Same conclusion, different number - do not quote one as if it were the only reading. (b) The protrusion skew curve's intermediate values differ between refuter-3's family and mine (at 10 degrees: 5.7334 vs 6.0169) because we walked different one-parameter paths through direction space. The endpoints are identical and the conclusion is unaffected, but neither intermediate series is canonical.

THE BIGGEST ERROR IN THE PRIOR RECORD WAS A PREMISE, NOT AN ARITHMETIC SLIP, AND SALVAGE DID NOT CATCH IT. Every dead lens and the surviving synthesizer accepted that z = 52.035 is a meaningful part boundary and then argued about what number to compute there. Only the adversarial phase asked whether the boundary exists at all - it does not. lens:geom actually tried to RESCUE the flawed exclusion with a bounding-box bound. This is a standing methodological warning for this project: re-derivation audits arithmetic well and premises badly, so the adversarial step is not optional garnish.

B7250 BEING 'ONE REAL PART' IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A CERTAINTY. Its closure (zero open edges) plus the fastener layout is strong, but it is a body in a CAD assembly export, and link5.stl demonstrably contains un-booleaned internal geometry (139 non-manifold edges, a doubled zero-thickness mating sheet). If the shipped fixed jaw is a separate moulding bonded or screwed inside that housing, then 103.8000 and 105.6842 bound nothing relevant and hypothesis D's real object is still unmeasured.

NOTHING HERE WAS WRITTEN TO THE REPO. This is a read-only analysis; all scratch work is in the session scratchpad at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-cgxr-Documents-Robotics-RoArm-Project/9797b497-1c0e-46a4-b44e-122794d900cf/scratchpad/synth_partial.txt (176 lines, appended incrementally after every established number so a mid-flight death would have left the evidence). No Gate-0 script was re-run and nothing under claudedocs/runtime_logs/grasp_track/g0b_d420/ was touched. The state_doc_edits_required list is a specification for a human or a later session to apply, not something I applied.

PROJECT-RULE FLAG, RAISED DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN BURIED. The AGENTS.md Session progress rule requires each research session to run at least one experiment that can fail, and forbids validation that cannot change a decision. This session did run falsifiable checks - and several failed, which is why verdicts moved. But it produced no physical experiment, and the natural next step (a bench gate) is precisely what I am recommending you NOT run until the instrument question is answered.
